forms.metaDescription: Contact form implementation examples for the localized template.
forms.title: Inquiry form implementation examples
forms.description: Two contact form styles were reintroduced on top of the i18n-aware branch: one with Server Actions and one with an API route.
forms.overviewActionDescription: Best when your Next.js app already owns the server and you want the shortest path from form to backend processing.
forms.overviewApiDescription: Best when you want a fetch-based frontend integration that can be separated from the server more easily.
forms.compareDescription: Both examples share the same validation, Turnstile verification, and Discord relay on the server side.
forms.comparePointOne: Use the Server Action route when the app is deployed as a full Next.js server.
forms.comparePointTwo: Use the API route when the UI may move to a separate host or needs an explicit HTTP boundary.
forms.comparePointThree: Both pages use the same localized field labels and validation feedback.
forms.actionMetaDescription: A localized contact form example powered by a Next.js Server Action.
forms.actionDescription: This version posts directly to a Server Action, keeping Turnstile verification and the Discord webhook entirely on the server.
forms.actionFeatureDescription: This is the shortest integration when your Next.js app already runs with server capabilities.
forms.actionFeaturePointOne: The form action points directly at a Server Action, so you do not need a separate client fetch step.
forms.actionFeaturePointTwo: The Turnstile secret and Discord webhook stay on the server and never reach the browser.
forms.actionFeaturePointThree: If you need a fetch-based boundary instead, compare it with the API version.
forms.apiMetaDescription: A localized contact form example that submits to an API route.
forms.apiDescription: This version submits via fetch to an API route, which makes the frontend/server boundary more explicit.
forms.apiFeatureDescription: This is easier to reuse when the UI and API need to be separated over time.
forms.apiFeaturePointOne: The client only needs to call an HTTP endpoint, which keeps the frontend integration portable.
forms.apiFeaturePointTwo: Turnstile verification and Discord delivery still happen on the server in the shared backend flow.
forms.apiFeaturePointThree: If you want the smallest Next.js-only setup, compare it with the Server Action version.
forms.cardActionDescription: A direct form action for server-first Next.js deployments.
forms.cardApiDescription: A fetch-based form for a clearer HTTP boundary.
